questions.questionTextEn: Generally the slope of demand curve is being :
questions.explanation: The law of demand expresses the relationship between the quantity demand of a commodity and its prices. According to the law of demand, the quantity demanded decreases with an increase in the price and increases with a fall/decrease in the price. Thus, this law expresses a inverse relationship between price and demand. The demand curve slopes downwards from left to right. The reason for the downwards movement of the demand curve from left to right is due to 'Diminishing marginal utility'.

questions.questionTextEn: The famous "Diamond-Water" paradox is explained by :
questions.explanation: Diamond Water Paradox:-This concept was propounded by Adam smith. this concept explains why diamond is expensive even though it is of little use and water which is very useful for life but has low cost. This notion makes it clear that the value of a commodity is determined neither by the amount of labor involved in its production, nor by the total utility of a commodity, but by the marginal utility derived from its consumption is determined by it. Water supply is very high. Due to the abundance of its supply, as its consumption increases, its marginal utility will be very less, therefore its value will be less, whereas incase of diamond, which has no utility, the will be a shortage of supply due to its rarity and as its consumption increases its value price will increase.

questions.questionText: Ricardo-Barro equivalence is related to :
questions.questionTextEn: Ricardo-Barro equivalence is related to :
questions.explanation: Ricardo- Barro equivalence is related to Fiscal policy. The Ricardo- Barro equivalence postulates that an Individual's saving behaviors is affected in the same way by government spending whether it is financial by taxes or public debt, both will be equivalent in terms of effect. According to this- (i) Changes in tax rates will have no effect on consumer expenditure because the taxpayers anticipates that a cut in the current tax rate will necessarily bring an increase in tax rate in future. (ii) Both tax and debt are equivalent in terms of effectiveness because public debt is a type of deferred tax.

questions.questionText: Leibenstein in his critical minimum effort thesis treats population as a factor that is :
questions.questionTextEn: Leibenstein in his critical minimum effort thesis treats population as a factor that is :
questions.explanation: In this theory of critical minimum effort, Liebenstein considers population as an income reducing factor this theory is based on the belief that the vicious circle of poverty and low capital formation is found in underdeveloped countries due to population pressures. These vicious circles remain vicious because the desired incentives or effort for development can not be made available insufficient quantity, then there is definitely an increase in income, but the increased income is consumed by the increased population. As a result the order of development remain stable. Therefore it is necessary that the investment should be mode in the minimum amount necessary so that economic by breaking the vicious circle, the path of economic development can be paved proponents of this approach are economists - Rosenstein Rolan, Regner Nurkse, Arthur Lewis and Nelson.
